news.headline: HBL unveils HBL PayPak UnionPay co-badge debit card; SBP governor hails launch
news.summary: HBL, described as Pakistan's largest debit-card issuer, launched the HBL PayPak UnionPay Co-Badge Debit Card at a ceremony at HBL Tower, Karachi, on Jul 15, 2026, developed with 1Link-operated PayPak and UnionPay International to combine domestic PayPak acceptance with UnionPay's international network on one card. SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad welcomed the launch as aligned with SBP's Vision 2028 and the 'Cashless Pakistan' agenda; no revenue, fee or volume figures for the card itself disclosed in the sources reviewed - reputational/strategic item for HBL, not caught in the prior checkpoint.

news.headline: Mobile banking users reach 137 million as digital payments surge
news.summary: Published 11:01am PKT, citing SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad: mobile banking users reached 137 million; retail digital transactions rose from 6.9bn to nearly 12bn over the past year; active merchants accepting digital payments rose from ~500,000 to over 2 million; remittances received via digital channels rose from 80% to 92%. Sector-wide digital-payments tailwind, no individual bank ticker figures disclosed.

news.source: Business Recorder / Express Tribune / PakTribune / Daily Patriot
news.headline: PSX extends rebound - KSE-100 up nearly 3,100 points by midday as oil stabilises
news.summary: Thursday afternoon, continuing from the morning's +2,604.49-point read already logged this cycle (previous close 175,285.78): Business Recorder reported the index at 178,378.43 as of 12:09pm, up 3,092.65 points (+1.76%); Express Tribune's midday report had it at 178,124.14, up 2,838.36 points (+1.62%), intraday high 178,431.73 / low 175,672.33, volume 144.6m shares worth Rs13.72bn; Daily Patriot reported an intraday high of 178,431.73 (+3,145.95 pts, +1.79%). Drivers: stabilising oil prices (Brent -0.5% to $84.50/bbl, still +11% for the week) as US-Iran Strait of Hormuz tensions eased, and softer US inflation data reducing Fed rate-hike fears; Business Recorder cited buying interest in automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil & gas exploration, OMCs, power generation and refinery; Daily Patriot noted an analyst comment that 'attention is shifting to the upcoming earnings season, which is expected to drive sector-specific activity.' No confirmed final closing-bell figure found in sources reviewed as of this cycle (17:00 PKT checkpoint) - flagged as the latest available intraday read pending a Closing Bell/DPS-confirmed print.

news.headline: KSE-100 confirmed close: index settles up 2,837.78 points as US-Iran dialogue hopes lift risk appetite
news.summary: Thursday final close confirmed, superseding the midday +3,092.65-point read logged in the prior checkpoint (previous close 175,285.78 on Wednesday): KSE-100 settled at 178,123.57, up 2,837.78 points (+1.62%); Express Tribune reported volume of 736.96m shares worth Rs34.61bn, 496 companies traded, 342 advancers vs 129 decliners vs 25 unchanged; Dawn separately reported volume 736.9m shares (+26.23% vs prior session) worth Rs34.5bn (+32.88%), intraday range 175,672 (low) to 178,431 (high). Driver per both: media reports of a possible resumption of US-Iran dialogue eased geopolitical concerns and improved risk appetite, extending the rebound from Tuesday's Strait-of-Hormuz selloff for a second straight session; Express Tribune also reported foreign investors bought a net Rs2.53bn of shares in the session.

news.headline: Lotte Chemical Pakistan (LOTCHEM) posts Q2CY26 EPS of Rs1.87, declares Rs1.50/share cash dividend
news.summary: LOTCHEM's PSX Data Portal (DPS) company page shows Q2 2026 (six months ended Jun 30, 2026) results announced Jul 16, 2026: Q2-alone EPS of Rs1.87 (vs Q1 2026 EPS of Rs0.97), Q2 sales of PKR 23.85bn (vs Q1's PKR 20.86bn) and Q2 profit-after-tax of PKR 2.84bn (vs Q1's PKR 1.47bn); DPS payouts section did not yet display a dividend record at the time reviewed. Express Tribune and Dawn both separately reported the results drove market momentum, quoting 'earnings per share (EPS) of Rs1.87 (up 192% year-on-year)' [Express Tribune] vs 'Q2CY26 results with earnings per share of Rs1.87 (up 192% quarter-on-quarter)' [Dawn] - the two outlets disagree on whether the 192% growth figure is YoY or QoQ, and both reported a cash dividend of Rs1.50/share not yet reflected in the DPS payouts page as of this review; Dawn additionally reported LOTCHEM was the day's top-volume stock at 70.0m shares traded. Logged as impact 4 (material earnings surprise + dividend announcement) per desk news-impact scale; the YoY-vs-QoQ discrepancy in the growth-rate comparison basis should be confirmed against the primary PSX filing in a follow-up cycle.

news.summary: Friday morning (this checkpoint's session, 9:35am PKT), reversing part of Thursday's 178,123.57 close: KSE-100 at 177,562.67, down 560.89 points (-0.31%), as renewed US-Iran tensions resurfaced and reversed some of Thursday's rebound momentum; selling observed across automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, fertiliser, oil & gas exploration, OMCs and power generation sectors, with index-heavy HUBCO, MARI, POL, PPL, MCB, MEBL, NBP and UBL trading in the red. news.headline: SBP forex reserves fall $1.245bn on debt repayments
news.summary: SBP-held reserves fell $1.245bn (-6.7% WoW) to $17.226bn in the week ended Jul 10, 2026, reversing most of the prior week's $1.944bn rise to $18.471bn (week ended Jul 3); SBP attributed the decline to 'repayments against external debt obligations'; total liquid foreign reserves (SBP $17.226bn + commercial banks $5.450bn) stood at $22.676bn. Published Jul 16, 2026 9:15pm PKT - missed in the prior checkpoint, logged now for completeness.

news.headline: KSE-100 confirmed Friday close: index reverses two-session rebound, ends down 2,320.78 points
news.summary: Confirmed final close per PSX's own market-summary page (psx.com.pk/market-summary/, page captured 2026-07-17 17:25:02 PKT, market status 'Closed'): KSE-100 settled at 175,802.78, down 2,320.78 points (-1.32%) from Thursday's confirmed close of 178,123.57; volume 621,024,167 shares across 372,786 trades. This erases most of the two-session rebound (Wed +1,766.97, Thu +2,837.78) and follows Friday's opening-session weakness already logged this cycle (Business Recorder: -560.89 pts / -0.31% at 9:35am) amid renewed US-Iran tension; the market recovered to +74.50 pts (178,198.06) by the 12pm first-session close per Business Recorder before giving it all back into the Friday afternoon session's official close. No closing-bell narrative article with sector/stock-level breakdown was located in sources reviewed as of this checkpoint (17:00 PKT); figure is PSX's own official confirmed print, logged per desk impact-4 threshold for a sharp reversal of the week's recovery.

news.headline: PSX Closing Bell: The Show Is Over
news.summary: Friday close detail (published 5:08pm PKT), corroborating and adding sector/stock breakdown to the PSX-official close already logged this cycle: KSE-100 settled at 175,802.78, down 2,320.78 points (-1.30%); Mettis reports KSE-100 volume 267.06m shares, value traded Rs29.88bn, 372,786 trades, breadth 101 gainers/367 decliners/29 unchanged. Top losers LOTCHEM -4.34%, AICL -3.71%, KTML -3.20%, PSX -3.19%, KEL -3.16%; top gainers HGFA +2.65%, CNERGY +1.98%, PGLC +1.53%, FHAM +1.00%, ATRL +0.43%. Mettis attributes the session's weakness to profit-taking after recent gains plus disappointing external-account data, quoting: 'Pakistan reported a current account deficit of $649 million in June, compared with a surplus of $220m in June last year' (broadly corroborated by a separate Samaa TV report of a roughly $650m June current-account deficit) - driving broad-based selling in Commercial Banks (-680.32 index points), Oil & Gas Exploration Companies (-327.46 points) and Cement (-266.14 points). Logged at impact 4: this current-account swing from surplus to deficit is the specific macro data point identified as today's session driver.

news.headline: PKR ends firmer against greenback
news.summary: Rupee closed at Rs277.96/USD in the interbank market Friday, up 1.20 paisa from Thursday's close of Rs277.97; intraday range Rs277.95 (high) to Rs278.00 (low).

news.headline: U.S.A. leads as top export destination for Pakistan in Jun
news.summary: Pakistan's exports to the US reached $539.66m in June 2026, up 12.9% YoY from $477.85m (June 2025) and up 17% MoM, retaining the US as Pakistan's top export destination; China ranked second at $247.58m (+19.7% YoY), UK third at $188.44m (+7.7% YoY), Germany fourth at $170.43m (+23% YoY).

news.headline: Meezan Bank strengthens sustainability agenda with LEED Gold Certification
news.summary: MEBL's Meezan Tower Islamabad (its new regional headquarters) was awarded LEED Gold Certification by the U.S. Green Building Council/Green Business Certification Inc., citing high-performance HVAC, energy-efficient lighting and intelligent building controls; no financial figures disclosed - reputational item, not financial.

news.headline: Gold price in Pakistan falls Rs3,600 per tola
news.summary: 24-karat gold in the domestic market fell Rs3,600 to Rs421,836 per tola on Friday (from Rs425,436 the previous day) per the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewelers Sarafa Association; silver also traded lower - background commodity item, no PSX-listed gold miner in the universe.
